correctness.rationale: Hub redraw at rate c contributes −cC to the generator (effective flip rate c/2); leaf i contributes ℓ_i(t_i C−σ_i). Acting on the two Walsh monomials for each subset gives the two triangular equations, with only lower-order terms in the numerators. Positivity of the spin-flip rates implies irreducibility, so inversion of configuration indicators indeed recovers the unique stationary law. The singleton and pair equations give the claimed positive cross-leaf correlations and the ratio 1+2c/(ℓ_i+ℓ_j). A leaf redraw changes only its bond contribution; the resulting mean energy inflow is J_iℓ_i(B_{i}−t_i), proving the individual negative current, hub balance and positive entropy production under the stated convention. For common leaf rate ℓ, conditional on the stationary hub past each leaf has mean t_i Z by its independent exponential age. An independent check of the beta law uses the generator on Z^k and CZ^k: E[C Z^k]=E[Z^{k+1}], and E[Z^{k+1}]=k E[Z^{k−1}]/(k+c/ℓ) for k≥1, with E[Z]=0. These are the moments of the claimed beta density and its sign-resolved law; compact support determines the distribution. The conditional variance of the homogeneous empirical mean is at most 1/n, giving the asserted limit and variance.
